Faiss's index types represent trade-offs among search time, search quality, memory used per index vector, training time, adding time, and the need for external data for unsupervised training. These trade-offs affect the efficiency and accuracy of similarity search, but they do not directly address the ranking quality of retrieved contexts.[S1]

Context Precision evaluates the retriever's ability to rank relevant chunks higher than irrelevant ones for a given query. It is calculated as the mean of precision@k for each chunk in the context, where precision@k is the ratio of relevant chunks at rank k to total chunks at rank k. This metric directly measures ranking quality.[S2]

Improving speed alone cannot establish better ranking because speed optimizations in Faiss focus on search efficiency (e.g., faster exact or approximate nearest neighbor search) but do not inherently improve the relevance ordering of results. Ranking quality is a separate dimension measured by metrics like Context Precision, which assesses how well relevant items are placed at the top of the retrieved list.[S1][S2]

cases.machine_answer:
LangGraph's persistence layer uses checkpointers to save graph state snapshots, which preserve an agent's workflow state across process restarts.
